descriptionChirho: A person who teaches or instructs, especially in a religious or authoritative context; used as a title of respect for Jesus (Greek didaskalos) and for teachers in the early church. Multilingual evidence confirms a unified sense across singular and plural: Spanish 'maestro/maestros,' Hindi 'guru/shikshak,' Arabic 'mu'allim/mu'allimin,' Korean 'seonsaengnim/gyosadeul,' Swahili 'mwalimu/walimu.' The singular forms frequently serve as a vocative title ('Teacher!') while the plural denotes the office or role of teachers in the community.
